title: Stepping Numbers
summary: Identify integers within a specified range [low, high] where the absolute difference between each pair of consecutive digits is exactly 1.
statement: Identify integers within a specified range [low, high] where the absolute difference between each pair of consecutive digits is exactly 1. Present these stepping numbers in ascending order.
constraints: Zero is a stepping number, and low and high are inclusive nonnegative bounds.
A positive number is stepping when every pair of adjacent digits differs by exactly one.
Return all stepping numbers in the interval; output order does not matter.
hints: Generate positive stepping numbers from one-digit seeds.
Append only last digit minus one and plus one when they remain decimal digits.
Record values inside the bounds and expand only values no greater than high; handle zero separately.
Every positive stepping number has one unique prefix chain from its first digit, so BFS generates all and only valid values.
editorial: Every positive stepping number has one unique prefix chain from its first digit, so BFS generates all and only valid values.

tests.explanation: The interval contains zero through nine, ten, twelve, and twenty-one.
Only ten and twelve have adjacent digits differing by one.
